promise.en: By the end, you will never forget the small word Mongolian doesn't have.
promise.mn: Энэ хичээлийн төгсгөлд монгол хэлэнд байхгүй жижиг үгийг хэзээ ч мартахгүй.

slides.say: A and an. Two of the smallest words in English, and two of the most common. Mongolian doesn't have them at all, which is exactly why they get a whole video.

explain.en: Look at the Mongolian: nothing stands where a and an are.
explain.mn: Монгол өгүүлбэрт a, an-ий оронд юу ч байхгүй.

slides.say: Read the English sentences. [click] Now look at the Mongolian. In the same place there is nothing. English puts a small word in front of one thing. Today: which one, a or an, and when.
slides.teach: Putting the Mongolian underneath makes the missing word visible, and visible is the point: students genuinely don't hear that it's missing when they speak.

explain.en: What is different about the second row?
explain.mn: Хоёр дахь мөрийн үгс юугаараа өөр вэ?

slides.say: Read both rows twice. Then ask: what is different about the words in the second row? Answer it: they all start with a, e, o or u.
slides.teach: It is tempting to say "vowel letter" here. Hold back; the letter-versus-sound twist comes on slide 5 and lands better as a surprise.

rows.chip: a cat, a book, a teacher
an apple, an egg, an orange

callout.en: The n joins the next word: an apple.
callout.mn: n дараагийн үгтэйгээ холбогдоно: an apple.

slides.say: The rule: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound. [click] The vowels are a, e, i, o, u. [click] Why does an exist at all? Try saying a apple. Two vowels crash into each other. The n builds a bridge: an apple. Listen: the n joins on to the next word, a-napple.
slides.teach: The bridge image is easy to remember and quietly teaches linking. Say an apple so the n clearly attaches forward.

explain.en: Your ears decide, not your eyes.

slides.say: Here is the puzzle. University starts with u. But listen: you-niversity. It starts with a you sound, and that is a consonant sound. So: a university. [click] Hour starts with h. But the h is silent: our. It starts with a vowel sound. So: an hour. Your ears decide, not your eyes.
slides.teach: Say each word slowly, exaggerating the first sound, then naturally. At A1 only four words really matter: university, uniform, hour, honest. This is also the slide that separates a good learner from a careful one.

callout.en: a and an look only at the next word.
callout.mn: a, an зөвхөн дараагийн үгээ хардаг.

slides.say: A and an only ever look at the very next word. Put an adjective in front and the choice can change. An apple, but a red apple. A car, but an old car.
slides.teach: Students learn "apple takes an" as a fixed pair and then write an red apple. This slide prevents that habit before it forms.

title.en: When we use a and an

slides.say: A and an mean one, any one. So we use them with a single thing you can count. [click] With jobs, English always needs a or an: He is a driver. In Mongolian we just say Тэр жолооч. [click] And because a means one, it can never go with a plural. A book, or books. Never a books.
slides.teach: Jobs are the biggest single source of missing articles for Mongolian speakers. Uncountable nouns (water, rice) are a separate lesson; if you mention them at all, one spoken line.

callout.en: In speech, a is a quick, soft "uh".
callout.mn: Ярианд a нь богино, сул "э" авиа.

callout.en: The stress goes on the noun.

slides.say: In normal speech, a is not ei. It is a tiny, quick uh: a cat, a book. And an is a quick un: an apple. The stress goes on the noun, never on the little word.
slides.teach: Mongolian learners often say ei every time, which sounds stiff. Model the weak form, exaggerated once, then naturally. Native speakers only say ei when stressing the number, as in I said A book, not two.

context.en: Mongolian has no a or an, so it is easy to forget.
context.mn: Монгол хэлэнд a, an байдаггүй тул амархан мартагддаг.

slides.say: First: jobs need a. [click] Second: a means one, so never with a plural. [click] Third: listen to the sound, not the letter.
slides.teach: For the second pair, add aloud that I have books is also correct; it just means more than one.

lines.en: I have **a** brother and **an** older sister.
lines.mn: Надад нэг дүү, нэг эгч бий.

lines.en: We have **a** dog and **an** old cat.
lines.mn: Манайд нохой, бас хөгшин муур бий.

slides.say: Read each line twice. For each highlighted word, say why: an engineer, vowel sound; an older sister, the adjective decides; a university, the you sound.
slides.teach: Every rule in the lesson appears once: vowel sound, consonant sound, jobs, an adjective changing the article, and the university trap.

cards.mn: a + гийгүүлэгч авиа · an + эгшиг авиа
Авиа шийднэ: an hour · a university

cards.en: Jobs need a or an: He is **a** driver.
cards.mn: Ажил мэргэжилд a, an заавал хэрэгтэй.

slides.say: Line one: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound. [click] Line two: the sound decides, not the letter. An hour, because the h is silent. A university, because it starts with a you sound. And only the very next word counts: an apple, but a red apple. [click] Line three: jobs always need a or an. In Mongolian, Тэр жолооч. In English, He is a driver. And in speech, a is a quick, soft uh. Close: Now you can talk about your family's jobs and describe single things without dropping the small word a Mongolian ear doesn't hear. [click] Closing line (spoken, never on the slide): Одоо энэ видеоны доорх дасгалаар мэдлэгээ шалгаарай. Hold the slide silently for three seconds.
slides.teach: Say every a on this slide as a weak uh, so the final thing students hear models the pronunciation as well as the rule. Hold the slide silently for three seconds after the closing sentence.
